title: Film Thickness Measurement - Missing Pattern Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Post-Deposition Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Maria Gonzalez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify Missing Pattern defects during post-deposition inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Missing Pattern defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: Film Thickness Measurement
- Target Defect: Missing Pattern
- Process Step: Post-Deposition
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-deposition monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v14.6.387
Recipe: FILM_THICKNESS_MEASUREMENT_28nm_POST_DEPOSITION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (182 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Film Thickness Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Missing Pattern defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 80 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 94% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.8% for Film Thickness Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.96 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-04-05
Wafers Tested: 50
Total Defects Found: 4487
Defect Density: 1428.26 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.4%
Capture Rate: 89.3%
Test Duration: 157 minutes
System Uptime: 99.4%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Missing Pattern at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The system successfully integrated with the factory automation host.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
